title: Customers from India, signed up in 2023
prompt: Select all columns for customers whose country is 'India' and whose signup_date is in 2023.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD') | orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD', amount REAL, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE country = 'India' AND signup_date >= '2023-01-01' AND signup_date < '2024-01-01' ORDER BY customer_id;

title: Customer count per country
prompt: For each country, count how many customers are from that country. Order the result alphabetically by country.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) | orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT country, COUNT(*) as customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY country;

title: Order amount for CASE-based order size
prompt: For every order, show order_id, amount, and a category column: 'small' if amount < 50, 'medium' if amount is between 50 and 200 inclusive, otherwise 'large'. Order by order_id.
expectedQuery: SELECT order_id, amount, CASE WHEN amount < 50 THEN 'small' WHEN amount <= 200 THEN 'medium' ELSE 'large' END as category FROM orders ORDER BY order_id;

title: Total spend for frequent customers
prompt: Find the total order amount per customer, but only include customers who have placed more than 2 orders. Show name and total_amount, ordered by name.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status) ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id
expectedQuery: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) as total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 2 ORDER BY c.name;

title: Customers who never ordered
prompt: List the names of customers who have never placed an order.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) LEFT JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name;

title: Deduplicate orders
prompt: The orders table has some exact-duplicate rows (same customer_id, order_date, and amount, from a data pipeline bug). Return one row per distinct (customer_id, order_date, amount) combination, keeping the smallest order_id when there are duplicates. Show order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, ordered by order_id.
expectedQuery: SELECT MIN(order_id) as order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id, order_date, amount ORDER BY order_id;

title: Most recent order per customer
prompt: For each customer who has placed at least one order, find their single most recent order: show name, order_date, and amount for that order. Order the result by name.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT name, order_date, amount FROM (SELECT c.name, o.order_date, o.amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_date DESC) as rn FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id) t WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY name;

title: Rank customers by total spend
prompt: Rank every customer by their total spend across all orders, highest first (customers with no orders count as $0). Show name, total_spend, and spend_rank.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) LEFT JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT name, total_spend, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_spend DESC) as spend_rank FROM (SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount),0) as total_spend FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name) t ORDER BY spend_rank;

title: Month-over-month order revenue change
prompt: Compute total order amount per calendar month (YYYY-MM), and the percentage change from the previous month (round to 1 decimal place). The first month should show NULL for pct_change. Show month, total, pct_change ordered by month.
schemaDescription: orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD', amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT month, total, ROUND(100.0*(total - LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month)) / LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month), 1) as pct_change FROM (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) as month, SUM(amount) as total FROM orders GROUP BY month) t ORDER BY month;

title: Above-average spenders (CTE)
prompt: Using a CTE, find customers whose total spend is strictly above the average total spend across ALL customers (customers with zero orders count as $0 and are included in the average). Show name and total_spend, ordered by total_spend descending.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) LEFT JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: WITH spend AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount),0) as total_spend FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name) SELECT name, total_spend FROM spend WHERE total_spend > (SELECT AVG(total_spend) FROM spend) ORDER BY total_spend DESC;

title: Running total of completed order revenue
prompt: For completed orders only, show order_id, order_date, amount, and a running total of amount ordered by order_date (ties broken by order_id ascending).
expectedQuery: SELECT order_id, order_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, order_id) as running_total FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' ORDER BY order_date, order_id;

title: Revenue share by country
prompt: For completed orders, show each country's total revenue and the percentage of total (all-country) revenue it represents, rounded to 1 decimal place. Order by pct_of_total descending.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: WITH rev AS (SELECT c.country as country, SUM(o.amount) as country_rev FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.country) SELECT country, country_rev, ROUND(100.0 * country_rev / (SELECT SUM(country_rev) FROM rev), 1) as pct_of_total FROM rev ORDER BY pct_of_total DESC;

title: Second-highest order amount per customer
prompt: For each customer, find their second-highest DISTINCT order amount (across all orders regardless of status). Customers with fewer than 2 distinct order amounts should not appear. Show name and second_highest_amount, ordered by name.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: WITH ranked AS (SELECT c.name as name, o.amount as amount, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_id ORDER BY o.amount DESC) as rnk FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id) SELECT DISTINCT name, amount as second_highest_amount FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 2 ORDER BY name;

title: Customers active in both January and February 2024
prompt: List the names of customers who placed at least one order in January 2024 AND at least one order in February 2024. Order by name.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o1 ON c.customer_id = o1.customer_id AND o1.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o1.order_date < '2024-02-01' JOIN orders o2 ON c.customer_id = o2.customer_id AND o2.order_date >= '2024-02-01' AND o2.order_date < '2024-03-01' ORDER BY c.name;

title: Spend quartiles across all customers
prompt: For every customer (including those with $0 in orders), compute total_spend and assign a spend_quartile from 1 (lowest) to 4 (highest) using NTILE(4) ordered by total_spend ascending. Show name, total_spend, spend_quartile ordered by total_spend.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) LEFT JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: WITH spend AS (SELECT c.customer_id as customer_id, c.name as name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) as total_spend FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name) SELECT name, total_spend, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_spend) as spend_quartile FROM spend ORDER BY total_spend;

title: First order date per customer vs signup date
prompt: For each customer who has placed at least one order, show name, signup_date, first_order_date (their earliest order_date), and days_to_first_order (the number of days between signup_date and their first order, as an integer). Order by name.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT c.name as name, c.signup_date as signup_date, MIN(o.order_date) as first_order_date, CAST(julianday(MIN(o.order_date)) - julianday(c.signup_date) AS INTEGER) as days_to_first_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name, c.signup_date ORDER BY c.name;

title: Countries where every customer has ordered
prompt: Find countries where EVERY customer from that country has placed at least one order (no customer from that country has zero orders). Show country, ordered alphabetically.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) LEFT JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: SELECT c.country FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.country HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 ORDER BY c.country;

title: Average order value per customer vs overall average
prompt: For each customer with at least one order, show name, avg_order_value (their average order amount, rounded to 2 decimals), and a flag above_overall_avg ('yes' or 'no') indicating whether their average order value exceeds the overall average order value across ALL orders. Order by name.
schemaDescription: customers(customer_id, name, country, signup_date) JOIN orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status)
expectedQuery: WITH per_customer AS (SELECT c.customer_id as customer_id, c.name as name, ROUND(AVG(o.amount), 2) as avg_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(amount) as overall_avg FROM orders) SELECT name, avg_order_value, CASE WHEN avg_order_value > (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall) THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END as above_overall_avg FROM per_customer ORDER BY name;
